name: Biology: Chemical Building Blocks of Life

notes.heading: Introduction to Chemical Building Blocks of Life
points: All living organisms are composed of chemical substances that form the basis of life
These substances are mainly organic and inorganic molecules
Carbon is the central element of life due to its ability to form stable bonds
Biomolecules include carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids
Water and minerals act as essential inorganic components

notes.heading: Carbohydrates
points: Carbohydrates are primary energy sources for living organisms
Composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in the ratio 1:2:1
Examples include glucose, starch, glycogen, and cellulose
Monosaccharides are simple sugars like glucose and fructose
Polysaccharides like starch and glycogen store energy in plants and animals respectively

notes.heading: Proteins
points: Proteins are made up of amino acids linked by peptide bonds
They perform structural, enzymatic, and regulatory functions
Examples include enzymes, hemoglobin, and antibodies
There are 20 standard amino acids forming various proteins
Protein structure has primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary levels

notes.heading: Lipids
points: Lipids are hydrophobic molecules including fats, oils, and waxes
They serve as long-term energy storage molecules
Phospholipids are key components of cell membranes
Steroids like cholesterol play regulatory roles in hormones
Lipids provide insulation and protection to organs

notes.heading: Nucleic Acids
points: Nucleic acids store and transmit genetic information
Two main types are DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) and RNA (Ribonucleic acid)
Made up of nucleotides containing sugar, phosphate, and nitrogenous base
DNA is double-stranded while RNA is usually single-stranded
Bases include Adenine, Thymine, Guanine, Cytosine, and Uracil (in RNA)

notes.heading: Water and Inorganic Ions
points: Water is the most abundant component of living cells
Acts as a universal solvent for biochemical reactions
Maintains temperature regulation in organisms
Minerals like calcium, potassium, sodium, and iron are essential
Ions help in nerve transmission, muscle contraction, and enzyme function

notes.heading: Enzymes
points: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of proteins
They speed up biochemical reactions without being consumed
Highly specific to substrates
Function depends on temperature and pH conditions
Examples include amylase, pepsin, and lipase
